_what_this_is: Manual frame-by-frame annotation of what is visible in each clip, by eye, at 2-second sampling. GROUND TRUTH for evaluating the detector. Never loaded by the app, never enters api_response.json, never reaches the custody ledger.
_method: ffmpeg fps=1/2 at 960px, every frame reviewed individually.
_sampling_caveat: 2s intervals. An action shorter than that can fall between frames.

clips.agreement: The 50-62s phone-consistent sequence and the 150-158s head turn are the two events most worth catching.

_corrections_to_earlier_claims: I previously called the Track-64 head turn a FALSE POSITIVE after looking at a single still where the subject faced forward. Reviewing the sequence at 72s, 76s and 80s shows a real lean-and-turn. The detector was right and I was wrong - a single frame cannot settle a temporal event.

I previously said a chit or paper is not resolvable at this resolution. A sheet held up in both hands IS clearly visible (clip 02, ~38s). A small folded chit probably is not, but that is a narrower claim than the one I made.
_real_events_the_detector_missed: Clip 02, 50-62s: woman with head down over an object held low - phone-consistent, sustained ~12s, and matches the clip's own title.
Clip 02, 150-158s: man in camo turning to look back over his shoulder.
_confirmed_false_positives: Clip 01, 88-118s: three hand_gesture findings in a window that is empty or shows people collecting belongings.
_context_that_changes_interpretation: Clip 02 shows a staff member with a lanyard actively assisting candidates and papers being handled openly. This is registration or verification, not a sealed exam - so papers in hand are probably legitimate there. Whether the phone-consistent sequence is an offence depends on the rules in force at that moment, which the footage cannot show.

_adjudications._what_this_is: Verdict on each SPECIFIC detection the detector raised, reached by re-extracting that frame from the source video at native 1280x720 and cropping to the bbox with padding. Separate from 'annotations', which record what is visible in the clip regardless of what the detector said. Needed because the annotations sample every 2s and do not cover every detection, and scoring an uncovered detection as wrong would be an assumption, not a measurement.
_adjudications._scale_note: bboxes in enriched_events.json are in 640x360 space; doubled to index native resolution.

_root_cause_found.finding: detectHandGestures in m8_9_golang/pose_analysis.go fires on a SINGLE frame whose wrist sits above the shoulder, with no minimum duration and no locomotion gate.
_root_cause_found.contrast: detectHeadTurns requires headTurnMinFrames=5 consecutive frames AND rejects the event when the subject travelled more than headTurnMaxLocomotion=2.0 shoulder-widths (pose_analysis.go:245, :282).
_root_cause_found.consequence: Anyone walking past with an arm raised - adjusting hair, carrying paper - trips it. 3 of the 6 confirmed false positives are people walking in the aisle; a 4th is a static resting posture that a duration gate would not fix but a seated-posture check would.
_root_cause_found.status: FIXED. detectHandGestures now requires the raise to persist across handRaiseMinFrames=3 sampled frames and rejects any subject who travelled more than handRaiseMaxLocomotion=2.0 shoulder-widths across the event, mirroring the two gates detectHeadTurns already had. Covered by m8_9_golang/pose_analysis_test.go.
_root_cause_found.not_addressed: The fourth false positive, a static resting posture, is untouched: neither gate applies to someone stationary with a hand genuinely above the shoulder line. That needs a seated-posture check, which the ankle occlusion noted at the top of pose_analysis.go makes unreliable at this resolution.
_root_cause_found.metrics_note: The precision and recall in the README were measured before this fix and have not been recomputed. Re-running evaluation/score.py needs the source footage and pipeline_out/, neither of which is in the repository.
